chapter: Leaving New York, jazz styles and religion
title: Becoming religious in 1952
summary: Smith says he was not religious then but now tries to stay on the right side, a change dating from 1952.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. It's something I was going to ask you before, but we got sidetracked. You were talking about getting advice when you were a traveling musician. You'd be staying in people's houses, and these religious people would say "A rolling stone gathers no moss."
Were you a religious man in those days?
A religious man? No. No. Truthfully...
But I get the impression that you are today.

Yeah, yeah. I try to stay on the other side of the fence now. I don't do right all the time. But I don't want to be on the other side of the fence. The Lord was good enough to let me come these many years! So he's waitin' on me. He's waitin' on me. So it's time to wake up and change.
When did you start to feel this way?
That's a long time. What happened to sort of turn you around?
